verdicts.text: Kubernetes is evolving to support AI through GPU-aware scheduling and more advanced workload orchestration.

Red Hat describes it as "Smarter GPU scheduling for AI workloads", and KubeDojo writes: "For AI workloads, DRA is the foundation for more advanced scheduling patterns" (Kueue, HAMi, Gateway API inference extension).
verdicts.framing_note: This is a broad qualitative trend claim with no cited source. Several independent 2025–2026 sources support it.

verdicts.text: According to Gartner, 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.

The 63% figure and the attribution are correct, but the claim recasts completed deployment as early adoption. Also, the claim drops the survey context (Q3 2023, 598 global respondents), which matters for 'currently' in a 2024-and-beyond post.

verdicts.text: The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is part of what makes direct action by AI assistants on infrastructure practical.
verdicts.evidence: (escalated from pass1) A July 2026 revision of MCP does exist. The spec was released as version 2026-07-28, and the official MCP blog says it brings "a stateless protocol core, Multi Round-Trip Requests, header-based routing... authorization hardening, a formal extensions framework". The date is correct. The part saying it makes AI assistants acting on infrastructure "practical" is the author's interpretation, but the release's focus on scaling and security reasonably supports it.
verdicts.framing_note: The factual anchor, a July 2026 MCP revision, is confirmed. The claim that it enables direct action on infrastructure is an editorial reading, and no source measures that.
verdicts.intuition_flag: This post is titled "10 trends shaping 2024", so it seems odd for it to mention a July 2026 spec release. The reviewer should check whether the update fits with the post's date and framing.
